extracted.intended_audience: students and writers learning composition and plain English style
extracted.subtask_description: A concise style guide (William Strunk Jr.'s The Elements of Style) listing elementary rules of usage, principles of composition, matters of form, and common word/orthography pitfalls to produce clear, vigorous English prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make definite assertions. Avoid tame, colorless, hesitating, non-committal language.—Rule 12
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocate for making definite assertions and steering clear of vague, timid, or non-committal phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form the possessive singular of nouns with ’s
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction to form possessive singular nouns using ’s (apostrophe + s).

rubrics_metrics.name: In a series of three or more terms with a single conjunction, use a comma after each term except the last
rubrics_metrics.description: Use commas to separate items in a series of three or more when joined by a single conjunction, placing a comma after each term except the final one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enclose parenthetic expressions between commas
rubrics_metrics.description: Set off parenthetic or interrupting expressions with commas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place a comma before and or but introducing an independent clause
rubrics_metrics.description: When 'and' or 'but' introduces an independent clause, place a comma before the conjunction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not join independent clauses by a comma
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using only a comma to join two independent clauses (i.e., guard against comma splices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not break sentences in two
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not improperly split sentences into two fragments; keep sentence structure whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: A participial phrase at the beginning of a sentence must refer to the grammatical subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure any participial phrase that opens a sentence grammatically refers to that sentence's subject (avoid dangling/misplaced modifiers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide words at line-ends, in accordance with their formation and pronunciation
rubrics_metrics.description: When hyphenating words at line breaks, divide them following their morphological formation and pronunciation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the paragraph the unit of composition: one paragraph to each topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat the paragraph as the basic unit of composition and limit each paragraph to a single topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: As a rule, begin each paragraph with a topic sentence; end it in conformity with the beginning
rubrics_metrics.description: Start paragraphs with a clear topic sentence and conclude them so they align with and support that opening idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the active voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer active-voice constructions over passive ones for clearer, more direct writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put statements in positive form
rubrics_metrics.description: Express statements positively rather than negatively when possible (avoid needless negation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit needless words
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove unnecessary words to achieve brevity and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid a succession of loose sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not string together many loose (paratactic) sentences; vary sentence structure and build cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express co-ordinate ideas in similar form
rubrics_metrics.description: Use parallel structure when expressing coordinate or comparable ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep related words together
rubrics_metrics.description: Place words that belong together close to each other to avoid ambiguity and misreading.

rubrics_metrics.name: In summaries, keep to one tense
rubrics_metrics.description: When summarizing, maintain a single tense throughout for consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place the emphatic words of a sentence at the end
rubrics_metrics.description: Position the most important (emphatic) words of a sentence toward its end for emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: A FEW MATTERS OF FORM
rubrics_metrics.description: Section heading indicating additional recommendations on matters of form (typography, manuscript form, punctuation conventions, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: WORDS AND EXPRESSIONS COMMONLY MISUSED
rubrics_metrics.description: Section heading listing words and expressions that are frequently misused, with corrections and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: WORDS COMMONLY MISSPELLED
rubrics_metrics.description: Section heading listing commonly misspelled words and their correct spellings.
